Session: `6679d191-11f4-465b-b322-0e0409d76793`

Worktree: `objectstack-issue-15163`

os-dev-report

## Verdict: a refusal reached by NO layer — a real defect, and it is wider than reads

On the single-kernel provider wiring under a live, non-degraded `isolated` posture:

- `organization_membership_ended` is reached by **no layer at all**. An API key stamped with an
  organization its owner is not a member of **reads that organization's rows and writes new rows
  into it**. HTTP 200 / HTTP 201.
- `organization_required` is reached by **no layer on reads** (HTTP 200, `total 0` — the exact
  silent-empty the refusal was filed to kill) and **is** reached on **writes**, by Layer 0 in
  plugin-security (HTTP 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, ADR-0123 D2).

So the card's first outcome does not hold. B-prime's conclusion ("something is skipped here") was
right; its reasoning ("the Layer 0 wall would silently not be enforced") was wrong in the direction
already measured — the wall IS enforced, and enforcing it is precisely what lets the ex-member
through, because under `isolated` the wall is `organization_id = tenantId` and `tenantId` is the
value the unvetted key supplied.

Measured on `1bc3c092a` (the `origin/main` at fetch time). All five files the reading depends on are
byte-identical on today's `origin/main` `a23603ea9`:

```
$ git diff --stat 1bc3c092a origin/main -- packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts \
    packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts \
    packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts \
    packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts
(no output)
```

## How the boot was composed

Three real `os serve` processes from `packages/cli/bin/run.js` (not `dist/index.js`), same throwaway
app, same seed, same `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`, differing only in whether a `kernel-manager`
service is registered:

```
OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL=owner@probe.local \
OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite OS_DATABASE_URL=file:./.objectstack/probe-subject.db \
node ../../packages/cli/bin/run.js serve -p 3163 --log-level info
```

All three booted the posture for real, not degraded:

```
INFO [security] tenancy posture 'isolated' — the Layer 0 organization wall is ACTIVE (organization_id = active organization)
INFO [probe15163] TENANCY posture=isolated isolationActive=true degraded=false
```

Seeded through the engine with `context: { isSystem: true }`:

```
INFO [probe15163] STORE probe_note rows=2 orgs=["org_alpha","org_alpha"]
INFO [probe15163] STORE sys_api_key rows=3 ids=["key_member","key_exmember","key_noorg"]
INFO [probe15163] STORE sys_member rows=1 pairs=[["u_member","org_alpha"]]
```

`key_member` and `key_exmember` both carry `active_organization_id: org_alpha`; only `u_member` has a
`sys_member` row. `key_noorg` carries no organization. `probe_note` is `public_read_write` so Layer 1
contributes nothing, and the app declares an `isDefault` permission set granting it, so RBAC is open
— the only thing that can hide a row is Layer 0.

**Stand-in, stated plainly.** `@objectstack/organizations` is cloud-private and resolves from nowhere
in this workspace, so the probe app declares a local package of that name whose `OrganizationsPlugin`
registers the `org-scoping` service and nothing else. That is a behavioural copy of the stand-in this
repo already ships for exactly this purpose (`SimulatedOrgScopingPlugin`,
`packages/verify/src/harness.ts:61`, mounted by `bootStack({ multiTenant: 'posture-only' })`), and
`org-scoping` registration is the single fact the open core probes
(`TenancyService.probeIsolation`, ADR-0093 D5). It activates the POSTURE, not a wall of its own —
which is what makes the reading a reading about the open core's three candidate layers. What it
cannot speak for is any refusal the real enterprise plugin might add on top; that is out of the open
core's reach either way.

## The matrix

`GET` and `POST` on `/api/v1/data/probe_note`, credential in `x-api-key`:

| credential | SUBJECT (no `kernel-manager`) | KM-ONLY (`kernel-manager`, never bound) | CONTROL (`kernel` bound) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| member of `org_alpha` (positive control) | GET 200 `total 2` · POST 201 | GET 200 `total 2` · POST 201 | GET 200 `total 2` · POST 201 |
| **ex-member**, key stamped `org_alpha` | **GET 200 `total 2`** · **POST 201** | **GET 200 `total 2`** · **POST 201** | GET 401 · POST 401 |
| **no organization** | GET 200 `total 0` · POST 403 | GET 200 `total 0` · POST 403 | GET 401 · POST 401 |
| no credential | GET 401 | — | — |

Raw:

```
############ SUBJECT — single-kernel provider wiring (no kernel-manager) (port 3163) ############
  GET  probe_raw_member_key     HTTP 200  total=2 ids=['note_a1', 'note_a2']
  GET  probe_raw_exmember_key   HTTP 200  total=2 ids=['note_a1', 'note_a2']
  GET  probe_raw_noorg_key      HTTP 200  total=0 ids=[]
  POST probe_raw_member_key     HTTP 201  code=None org=org_alpha id=Z4BIfXqYrPXkz39Q
  POST probe_raw_exmember_key   HTTP 201  code=None org=org_alpha id=p2ra-XQfes4O4CJJ
  POST probe_raw_noorg_key      HTTP 403  code=PERMISSION_DENIED org=None id=None
############ CONTROL — multi-kernel wiring (kernel bound) (port 3164) ############
  GET  probe_raw_member_key     HTTP 200  total=2 ids=['note_a1', 'note_a2']
  GET  probe_raw_exmember_key   HTTP 401  code=UNAUTHENTICATED Authentication is required to access this endpoint.
  GET  probe_raw_noorg_key      HTTP 401  code=UNAUTHENTICATED Authentication is required to access this endpoint.
  POST probe_raw_member_key     HTTP 201  code=None org=org_alpha id=oEl_hounfB7LgerW
  POST probe_raw_exmember_key   HTTP 401  code=UNAUTHENTICATED org=None id=None
  POST probe_raw_noorg_key      HTTP 401  code=UNAUTHENTICATED org=None id=None
```

## 1. The ex-member key — reaches data, refused by no layer

`GET` returns both `org_alpha` rows. `POST` lands a row **inside `org_alpha`**, read back through the
legitimate member's key:

```
total: 4
   note_a1            | org: org_alpha | created_by: None       | name: alpha note 1
   note_a2            | org: org_alpha | created_by: None       | name: alpha note 2
   Z4BIfXqYrPXkz39Q   | org: org_alpha | created_by: u_member   | name: w-probe_raw_member_key
   p2ra-XQfes4O4CJJ   | org: org_alpha | created_by: u_exmember | name: w-probe_raw_exmember_key
```

Which layer could have refused, and why none did:

- **better-auth session validation** — never consulted. `resolveAuthzContext`
  (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:271`) takes the API-key branch first and the
  session path is `if (!userId && ...)`, already satisfied.
- **REST `computeExecCtx` posture branch** — `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:2401-2407`. This is
  the skip; see section 4.
- **Layer 0 in plugin-security** — `computeTenantLayer0Filter`,
  `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts:114`. It ran, and it **passed the caller**.
  Under `isolated` it is `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts:145-147`:
  ```ts
  // `isolated`: the hard wall. Missing active org → fail closed.
  if (!input.organizationId) return { ...RLS_DENY_FILTER };
  return { organization_id: input.organizationId };
  ```
  `organizationId` is `ExecutionContext.tenantId`, and on this wiring `tenantId` is
  `sys_api_key.active_organization_id` copied through verbatim
  (`packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts:277`). The wall therefore compiles to
  `organization_id = org_alpha` — the caller's own claim, checked against nothing. Layer 0 under
  `isolated` deliberately never reads `accessible_org_ids` (that set is the `group` wall,
  `tenant-layer.ts:135-141`), so the one fact that would expose the ended membership is not an input
  to the layer that could act on it.

That division of labour is coherent as designed: the membership cross-check is not Layer 0's job,
it is `resolveAuthzContext`'s (`resolve-authz-context.ts:341-343`), and it is gated on
`input.tenancyPosture` — which this wiring never supplies.

## 2. The org-less key — no refusal on reads, a real refusal on writes

- **GET**: HTTP 200, `total 0`. `tenantId` is `undefined`, so Layer 0 returns `RLS_DENY_FILTER`
  (`tenant-layer.ts:146`) and the read resolves to nothing. Not a refusal: a 200 with an empty page,
  which is verbatim the `200 + total 0` silent-empty the `organization_required` refusal exists to
  replace.
- **POST**: HTTP 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and this one **is** a real refusal reached by another
  layer — plugin-security's ADR-0123 D2 write guard,
  `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` (`isTenantWallDenial` over the Layer 0
  filter, then `PermissionDeniedError`):
  ```
  [Security] Access denied: 'probe_note' is scoped to an organization, and this session has no
  active organization — so this insert has no organization to place the record in. Join or select
  an active organization and retry.
  ```

So for `organization_required` the answer is split, and only the write half is covered.

## 3. Control — the probe can show a refusal where one exists

Adding a `kernel-manager` (plus a `default-project` so a request resolves to an environment id)
flips **both** cases to 401 on the very same app, seed and posture, while the healthy member key
still returns 200 with two records. A probe that could not produce a refusal would have measured
nothing; this one does.

I added a third arm the card did not ask for, because it isolates the mechanism from the wiring
label. **KM-ONLY** registers a `kernel-manager` and *no* `default-project`, so
`resolveRequestEnvironmentId` yields `undefined`, neither kernel branch binds `kernel`, and the
behaviour is byte-identical to SUBJECT. The trigger is therefore precisely **`kernel` being bound in
`computeExecCtx`**, not "a `kernel-manager` service exists" — which also means B-prime's boot check
(presence of the service) was not even the right predicate for its own premise.

Census on `1bc3c092a`, confirming SUBJECT is the only wiring the open core can build:

```
$ git grep -n "registerService('kernel-manager'|registerService(\"kernel-manager\"|'kernel-manager':" -- packages/** apps/** examples/**
packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.test.ts:110
packages/cloud-connection/src/error-envelope.conformance.test.ts:183
packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts:122
packages/rest/src/rest-env-resolution.test.ts:460
packages/rest/src/rest-resolve-environment-single-window.test.ts:198
```

Five hits, all tests. Positive control, same grep shape for `org-scoping`: four hits — also all
tests/harnesses here, because the real registrar is the cloud-private package the stand-in replaces.

## 4. `computeExecCtx`, from the code

`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:2240`. Three branches can resolve an auth service; only the first
two bind `kernel`:

```ts
2263  if (environmentId && environmentId !== 'platform' && this.kernelManager) {
2264      kernel = await this.kernelManager.getOrCreate(environmentId);
...
2268  if (!authService && this.defaultEnvironmentIdProvider && this.kernelManager) {
2271          kernel = await this.kernelManager.getOrCreate(def);
...
2287  if (!authService && this.authServiceProvider) {          // the single-kernel branch
2288      authService = await seamOrUndefined(() => this.authServiceProvider!(environmentId));
```

The single-kernel branch resolves `authService` from `ctx.getService('auth')`
(`packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts:276`) and leaves `kernel` `undefined`. The posture is the one
input read off `kernel`:

```ts
2401  let tenancyPosture;
2402  try {
2404      tenancyPosture = effectiveTenancyPosture(await kernel.getServiceAsync('tenancy') as any);
2405  } catch {
2406      tenancyPosture = undefined;
2407  }
```

With `kernel` `undefined`, line 2404 throws a `TypeError` on property access before any service
lookup happens, the `catch` absorbs it, and `tenancyPosture` is `undefined`.

**Derived on this branch without a posture** (all of it, and all of it correct): `authService` and
therefore session validation; `ql` via `objectQLProvider`
(`rest-api-plugin.ts:321`, the local kernel's `objectql`); and out of `resolveAuthzContext` at line
2418 — `userId`, `tenantId`, `permissions` (key scopes plus permission sets), `positions`,
`systemPermissions`, `org_user_ids`, `accessible_org_ids`, `email`, the ADR-0095 `posture` rung;
plus `localization`, the ADR-0069 `authGate`, and `__authEnvironmentId`.

**Cannot be derived at all**: `tenancyPosture` — the only authorization input this branch sources
from `kernel`. (`__kernel` is also unavailable, but its own docblock says it is not an authorization
input.) Everything downstream follows mechanically:

- `resolveApiKeyAdmission` skips the org-less refusal, `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts:305`:
  `if (!tenantId && tenancyPosture)`.
- `resolveAuthzContext` skips the ex-member refusal, `resolve-authz-context.ts:341`:
  `if (keyPrincipal?.tenantId && input.tenancyPosture)`.

Both are guarded on the posture being present, and the absent-posture default is a documented,
deliberate ADMIT (`api-key.ts:257-263`): *"An ABSENT posture means 'the caller could not tell us
which posture is in force', and the answer to that is to admit ... refusing on an unknown posture
would break every org-less key on every `single` deployment whose transport has not been wired."*
The measurement's sharpest point is against that justification's premise: the transport it calls
"not yet wired" is not a residual case, it is **every** deployment the open core can build.

One more thing worth knowing before anyone reads the control's 401 as a good error: `authRefusal` has
no consumer. Outside its own module the only hits on `1bc3c092a` are two assertions in
`packages/rest/src/execctx-authz-input-seam-reachability.test.ts`. Both refusals surface by leaving
`userId` unset, so `computeExecCtx` returns `undefined` and `enforceAuth`
(`rest-server.ts:1527`) answers the generic anonymous 401 — byte-identical to sending no credential
at all. The refusal messages the two sites compose are never rendered anywhere.

## Blast radius

Every wall-enforcing `os serve` deployment the open core can build — `isolated` and `group`, since
both satisfy `postureEnforcesWall` — reaches neither API-key admission refusal on the read path.
Concretely, an API key outlives the membership that justified it: after a `sys_member` row is
deleted, a SCIM deprovision, a better-auth org removal or an ADR-0091 validity window lapsing, the
key keeps full read **and write** access to that organization until someone revokes the key by hand.
Verify-time membership checking was chosen over revoke-on-removal precisely because "a revoke-on-
removal hook has to catch EVERY one of those or it silently misses"
(`resolve-authz-context.ts:322-331`) — and on this wiring the verify-time check never runs, so the
deployment is back to the failure mode that reasoning rejected.

Not affected: `single` deployments (no wall, nothing to cross); the write path for an org-less key
(Layer 0 refuses, 403); the multi-kernel wiring (both refusals fire).

Per the card, no code and no PR — this is the reading only. The repair the outcome section names is
to make the single-kernel branch derive the posture, and I would add one thing to whatever card
picks that up: `authRefusal` needs a consumer in the same change, or the fix arrives as a 401 that
is indistinguishable from an unauthenticated request and tells the operator nothing about the ended
membership.

## Reproduction

Throwaway probe, never committed, worktree removed. To rebuild it: a `defineStack` app with one
`public_read_write` object and an `isDefault` permission set granting it; a config `plugins: [...]`
entry that seeds `sys_user` / `sys_organization` / `sys_member` / `sys_api_key` / rows on
`kernel:ready` through `context: { isSystem: true }`, and — for the control arms only — registers
`kernel-manager` and `default-project` in `init()`; plus a local package named
`@objectstack/organizations` exporting an `OrganizationsPlugin` that registers `org-scoping`.

**Measurement delivered — closing.** The reading is comment 5537114769 above; no code landed under this card, as its scope required.

**Outcome: the second of the two this card named — a refusal reached by NO layer**, and wider than the card anticipated. It scoped the question to two API-key admission refusals; the measurement found an ex-member's key both **reads and writes** another organization's rows on the single-kernel wiring under `isolated`, with a written row landing stamped `org_alpha`.

⇒ The docs-card outcome ("the wiring carries no posture and needs none") does **not** apply. Filed as **#15256**, `p0 · security · needs-user-decision`, because the repair — making the single-kernel branch derive the posture — is the option the 2026-09-02 ruling explicitly declined, so it is a re-ruling and ⛔ not a dispatch this seat can make.

**Carried into #15256 rather than lost here:**

- The mechanism, re-verified by this seat on `origin/main` after the report: `isolated`'s Layer 0 compares `organization_id` to the caller's active org and never reads `accessible_org_ids`; `tenantId` is `active_organization_id` copied verbatim off the key; and both posture-gated guards need a `tenancyPosture` the single-kernel branch never derives.
- The trigger is `kernel` being **bound** in `computeExecCtx`, not `kernel-manager` being present — measured by a third arm this card did not ask for (KM-ONLY), and it means **B′'s boot check tested the wrong predicate for its own premise**. ⛔ A boot refusal stays excluded as a remedy regardless.
- `authRefusal` has **zero** consumers, so deriving the posture on its own would convert a silent leak into a 401 indistinguishable from sending no credential. That is question 2 on #15256, deliberately not a separate card.
- ⚠️ **The scope limit that sizes the whole thing**: the probe used a local stand-in for the cloud-private `@objectstack/organizations` (a behavioural copy of `SimulatedOrgScopingPlugin`), so this reading covers the three open-core layers only. Whether the real enterprise plugin refuses is **step 1** of #15256 and decides whether the blast radius is open-core self-hosters or every walled deployment.

B′'s question, moved here when the maintainer withdrew the boot refusal from PR #15020, is answered: the wiring skips more than anyone had measured, and the answer is a defect rather than a docblock.

`pm:dispatched` stripped in the same stroke as the close; `domain:cli` retained.
